chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Saeed ibn Abdullah al-A'raj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who recites the Quran, then forgets it, then recites it, then forgets it. Is there any blame upon him for it? He said: No.
ai.seo_question: Is there a penalty for forgetting the Quran after reciting it?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the natural process of memorization and forgetting does not incur spiritual penalty (haraj), emphasizing ease in religious practice. It reflects the Shia scholarly principle that divine law accommodates human cognitive limitations, ensuring that the act of recitation remains valid even if retention is imperfect. This ruling reassures believers that consistent effort in recitation is valued over flawless memorization.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Saeed Bin Abdullah Al A’araj who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who recites the Quran, then forgets it. Then he recites it, then he forgets it. Would there be a blame upon him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 24. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Safwan from Sa’id ibn ‘Abd Allah al-A’Raj who has said the following: “
Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) about a man who reads the Holy Quran but then he forgets, he reads again and forgets. Is it an offense? The Imam said, ‘No, it is not an offense.’”
